scenario: Data staging + scheduled-task persistence + HTTPS exfiltration + cleanup
summary: On 2026-09-11, PowerShell on WS-DEV-02 launched 7z.exe which archived the user's Q3 spreadsheets into a password-protected 176 MB stage.7z in Temp. PowerShell then dropped sync.ps1 and created a logon scheduled task 'OneDriveSync' (TaskCache registry entry). Six outbound HTTPS connections followed to 203.0.113.77 (sync-cdn.example) from the same PowerShell process, after which stage.7z was deleted (cleanup).
kill_chain: 10:05 powershell.exe spawned by explorer.exe on WS-DEV-02
10:06 7z.exe spawned by powershell.exe: archiving C:\Users\dev02\Documents\Q3\*.xlsx with password
10:09 stage.7z (176 MB) created in C:\Users\dev02\AppData\Local\Temp by 7z.exe
10:16 sync.ps1 (2 KB) dropped to Temp by powershell.exe
10:16 schtasks.exe (child of powershell.exe) created scheduled task 'OneDriveSync' (/sc onlogon); TaskCache registry entry
10:25-10:47 six outbound HTTPS (443/tcp) connections by powershell.exe to 203.0.113.77 (sync-cdn.example)
key_iocs: stage.7z 176 MB in Temp, later deleted
evidence_basis: repeated exfiltration connections to external host
distractors: One benign failed-then-successful interactive (type 2, Kerberos) logon pair in the afternoon noise — tests that the agent does not over-conclude from the SCN-005-style pattern.
notes: All event severities are 1 (as in the original dataset); the agent must correlate behavior, not severity. Byte counts are not in telemetry — the agent should reason from connection count/timing and archive size/deletion.
